description.narrative: The overall objective of the ASDSP is "to transform Kenya's agric. sector into an innovative, commercially oriented, competitive and modem industry that will contribute to poverty reduction and improved food security in rural and urban Kenya". There are three components, sector coordination, natural resource management and value chains. The programme is for 5 yrs with Sida contribution of 350 MSEK.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2016Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: Significant results attained towards realization of the intended outcome include: Component 1: Establishment of the Transformation Initiative as the mode of sector coordination and operationalization of the Intergovernmental Secretariat (IGS) with functional Technical Working Groups to enhance National/County governments coordination; formation of 485 functional value chain partnerships through which extended value chain concepts were implemented; finalization of a functional MIS for programme monitoring; development of a sector M&E framework; and support to development of the new Agricultural Policy.
Component 2: About 58,000 (67% males, 33% adult females and youth) Value Chain Actors trained on NRM/CC related risk out of which 26,500 were linked to weather/climate information and using climate smart technologies (69% adult males, 31% adult females and youth); linkage/involvement of local Value Chain Actors in weather information dissemination and development of climate risk management plans; and linkage of over 4000 vulnerable Value Chain Actors to private and public social protection service providers.
Component 3: Support of 152 county partnership projects on capacity building of value organizations valued at BKES 1 (with ASDSP contributing 38% to leverage partners resources); 152 investments by value chain actors were implemented through the extended concepts coordinated by the Value Chain Platforms; development of 5 additional financial products in collaboration with Kenya Commercial Bank (a Sida/USAID credit Guarantee partner); support to development and establishment of 3 agro-value chain technology incubation centres; and development of a value chain micro site prototype to disseminate value chain based information, linking agro producers to agro trader’s.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
